newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana refinery set to reopen end Q2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ghana refinery set to reopen end Q2 1997.

text.p: Ghana's state-owned Tema Oil Refinery is on course to reopen on schedule at the end of the second quarter of 1997 following a $55 million rehabilitation and expansion project, a manager at the refinery said.
The closure in January of the refinery for six months has forced Ghana to import all its petroleum products.

"We are very, very on schedule. Mechanical completion is around the corner. The place is buzzing with South Koreans and Thais who are working around the clock," Emmanuel Quartey, the refinery production planning and control manager, told Reuters.
The work, which is being carried out by Samsung-Sunkyong Engineering Construction from South Korea, will increase capacity by 61 percent to 45,000 barrels per day.
"We hope to start up the revamped refinery by the end of the second quarter, when contracts for the supply of finished products expire," said Quartey.
"What is left to be done are minor works. We are mopping up."
Samsung helped fund the project with a $40 million loan, Quartey said. Tema Oil Refinery raised the remaining $15 million.
Quartey said imports were bought on a quarterly basis because of price fluctuations.
"We have quite a spectrum of traders and suppliers from all over the world who were selected by competitive tender," he added.
Normally Ghana imports about 1.3 million tonnes of crude oil and 0.3 million tonnes of finished petroleum products, mainly from Nigeria.
The refinery is listed for privatisation but Quartey suggested that it was unlikely to happen in the near future. "From where I stand I should say that privatisation is in the deep freezer," he said.
